facts.heading: Anxiety worsened in September
facts.content: Hannah feels anxious all the time, and this anxiety worsened in September.
facts.evidence: I think I'm just anxious all the time and it's got worse in September.

facts.heading: Hannah's teaching experience
facts.content: Hannah has taught at her school for 11 years.
facts.evidence: I've taught here for 11 years

facts.heading: Hannah's new role
facts.content: Hannah was the deputy head at her school.
facts.evidence: I was my deputy head at my school.

facts.heading: New role started in September
facts.content: Hannah was asked to step up into a new role when the deputy left in September.
facts.evidence: And then the head asked me to step up and when our deputy left.

facts.heading: Fear of being exposed as incompetent
facts.content: Hannah worries that people will notice she doesn't know what she is doing.
facts.evidence: I keep thinking they picked the wrong person and that sooner or later someone will notice I have no idea what I'm doing.

facts.heading: Anxiety on Sunday evenings
facts.content: Hannah experiences chest tightness and rehearsing meetings on Sunday evenings.
facts.evidence: Mostly Sunday evenings. My chest goes tight and I start rehearsing Monday's stuff meeting in my head.

facts.heading: Rehearsing worst-case scenarios
facts.content: Hannah rehearses every possible question and what people might think if she gets it wrong.
facts.evidence: Every possible question someone might ask and what I would say and what they would think of me if I got it wrong

facts.heading: Fear of being perceived as incapable
facts.content: Hannah fears people think she is out of her depth or that the job went to a teacher who can't read.
facts.evidence: That I'm out of my depth, that they gave the job to a nice ear for a teacher who can't actually read

facts.heading: Recent email rewriting
facts.content: Hannah rewrote the same email to the governors four times last week.
facts.evidence: Last week I rewrote the same email to the governors four times.

facts.heading: Fear of Mr. Hargraves' judgment
facts.content: Hannah was afraid Mr. Hargraves, the chair of governors, would think she was stupid regarding the behavior policy email.
facts.evidence: I was afraid Mr. Hargraves, the chair of governors, would think that I was stupid.

facts.heading: Mr. Hargraves' positive feedback
facts.content: Mr. Hargraves told Hannah in September that he was delighted.
facts.evidence: He told me in September he was delighted.

facts.heading: Feeling of inauthenticity
facts.content: Hannah feels like she is lying to Mr. Hargraves about being capable.
facts.evidence: Lying to him about being capable, as if I'm pretending.

facts.heading: Feeling like an imitation
facts.content: Hannah feels like a child wearing her mother's coat.
facts.evidence: Most days I feel like a child wearing her mother's coat.

facts.heading: Mother's professional background
facts.content: Hannah's mother was a head teacher for 20 years.
facts.evidence: She was a head teacher for 20 years.

facts.heading: Mother's retirement and legacy
facts.content: Hannah's mother retired six years ago and a library was named after her.
facts.evidence: She retired six years ago and they have named a library after her.

facts.heading: Comparing self to mother
facts.content: Hannah constantly compares her work to her mother's and wonders if she would have done it better.
facts.evidence: Everything I do, I think would she have done it better?

facts.heading: Mother's supportive advice
facts.content: Hannah's mother tells her she worries too much and should stop being silly.
facts.evidence: She says I've always worried too much and I should stop being silly.

facts.heading: Suppressing feelings due to mother's advice
facts.content: Hannah feels she doesn't tell her mother how bad things are because of her mother's advice.
facts.evidence: It makes me feel like I'm making a fuss, so I don't tell her how bad it is.

facts.heading: Waking at 4 AM daily
facts.content: Hannah is awake at 4 AM every morning.
facts.evidence: I'm awake at 4 every morning

facts.heading: Waking up with to-do list
facts.content: Hannah wakes up at 4 AM going through a to-do list that includes various concerns.
facts.evidence: Then I'm awake at 4 going through the to-do list

facts.heading: Waking since second week of term
facts.content: Hannah has been waking like this since about the second week of term.
facts.evidence: Since about the second week of term

facts.heading: Consumes five or six cups coffee
facts.content: Hannah drinks five or six cups of coffee to get through the day.
facts.evidence: Five or six

facts.heading: Physical symptoms in afternoons
facts.content: Hannah experiences a fast heart rate and shaky hands in the afternoons.
facts.evidence: My heart goes fast. My hands are a bit shaky

facts.heading: Had to leave meeting last Thursday

facts.evidence: Last Thursday I had to leave a meeting to splash my face with water

facts.heading: Feels exhausted from pretending
facts.content: Hannah feels exhausted by the end of every day from pretending.
facts.evidence: I am exhausted by the end of every day. Just from pretending.

facts.heading: Partner Ben's perspective
facts.content: Hannah's partner Ben believes she should just enjoy it.
facts.evidence: He says I should just enjoy it.

facts.heading: Feels guilty and alone
facts.content: Hannah feels guilty and a bit alone when Ben tells her to enjoy it.
facts.evidence: Guilty and a bit alone

facts.heading: Lost friends after promotion
facts.content: Hannah lost some company with the promotion.
facts.evidence: So you lost some company along with the promotion?

facts.heading: Misses children and class
facts.content: Hannah misses the children and her class.
facts.evidence: I miss them. I miss my class too.

facts.heading: Misses daily child interactions
facts.content: Hannah misses the daily experience of a child getting something for the first time.
facts.evidence: The daily bit where a child gets something for the first time.

facts.heading: Accepted promotion reluctantly
facts.content: Hannah said yes to the promotion because she couldn't say no to the head.
facts.evidence: I said yes in the room because I couldn't say no to her.

facts.heading: Cried after accepting promotion
facts.content: Hannah cried after accepting the promotion.
facts.evidence: Then I went home and cried.

facts.heading: Regrets leaving teaching
facts.content: Hannah felt that a year of teaching was something she would never get back.
facts.evidence: A year I think. And that I would never get to go back.

facts.heading: Felt unsupported by others
facts.content: Hannah felt that nobody asked her how she was feeling, only said well done.
facts.evidence: Nobody has asked me that. They just say well done.

facts.heading: Relaxed during summer holidays

facts.evidence: These summer holidays. We went walking in the lakes and I didn't think about school once for 10 days.

facts.heading: Pre-term week felt like a wreck

facts.evidence: The week before term, I was a wreck again. I couldn't eat on the Sunday.

facts.evidence: I would like to do the job without feeling like a fraud.

facts.evidence: Walking into a meeting and not rehearsing at first.

facts.content: Hannah wants to send an email only once.

facts.evidence: Being able to sit on the sofa in the evening without my stomach in knots.

facts.evidence: It helped for about two weeks and then I stopped

facts.evidence: put it by the kettle so I don't forget.
